modules.why: The person who dials 100 times when 99 say no. Everything else runs on this.
modules.job: Dial on a bad day without negotiating with yourself.

modules.why: Knowing is cheap. This module is about doing it every day: design, tracking, debriefs, calm decisions.
modules.job: Hit your dial target 5 days in a row, with a 2-line debrief after each block.

modules.why: Where you are on the map decides what you study and what you ignore.
modules.job: Name your stage, your one constraint and your best customer in one breath.

modules.why: Owners buy from people who understand their world: turnover, the first 90 days, Florida rules.
modules.job: Ask 3 owners about their turnover or first-90-day losses, and write down their numbers.

modules.why: Most calls die in the opener. Detachment, permission, one sentence, the right tone.
modules.job: Get past the opener into a real conversation on 3 calls in a row.

modules.why: The rep who asks most closes most. Find the pain in their words.
modules.job: Run a discovery that ends with the owner saying their problem and its cost out loud.

modules.why: Every no is a missing piece of value, certainty or urgency. Close with the price and the silence.
modules.job: Handle 3 different objections on real calls without arguing, and ask for the next step every time.

modules.why: An offer so good owners feel stupid saying no. Calls get easier when the offer is right.
modules.job: Pitch First Hire Free → Priority Bench with value, guarantee and a real limit, in under 2 minutes.

modules.why: Leads are the oxygen. Your channel is the phone, done at volume, with follow-up.
modules.job: Run a full day of dials + voicemails + follow-ups with a sequence.

modules.why: How to get paid so customers fund their own acquisition. Three numbers rule the business.
modules.job: Do the CAC, gross profit and payback maths for Caregiver Bench from memory.

modules.why: Once the calls work: lead magnets, content, referrals, partners and VSLs multiply them.
modules.job: Design one lead magnet and one referral ask for agency owners.

modules.why: The long middle: loneliness, bad months, other people's opinions. This keeps you in the game.
modules.job: Use one of these on a real bad day and write what happened.

modules.why: Hiring, delegating, systems, culture and speed. How one person becomes a company.
modules.job: Write the first role you would hire, its workflow, its delegation zones and its number.

modules.why: Decisions, incentives and leverage: how $20k MRR becomes $100M without blowing up.
modules.job: Write the 5 ways you could guarantee failure by 1 July, and what you do instead.

modules.why: What to do with the money so it stays and compounds. Educational, not financial advice.
modules.job: Know your current money milestone and the next one.

modules.why: Every other module runs on energy. Sleep is #1 in your cut order.
modules.job: Same bedtime and wake time for 7 days straight, caffeine before noon.

modules.why: Identity, the 4 laws and never missing twice: how a plan becomes automatic.
modules.job: Redesign one habit you keep skipping with the 4 laws and keep it 7 days.

modules.why: How to study so it sticks: recall, mixing, deep blocks. For BAC and for this Bootcamp.
modules.job: Do 3 BAC sessions this week with recall + interleaving, phone out of the room.

modules.why: Training that builds what you want: power for tennis, size for 85 kg, a body that lasts.
modules.job: Write the goal at the top of each session this week and log your 7-day weight average.

modules.why: Speed, power, shoulders, match plans and the inner game, for your play and your coaching.
modules.job: Play one match or set with a written plan A and plan B, and debrief it.

modules.why: Influence, reading people and handling friction: useful on calls, on court and at home.
modules.job: Use one influence principle honestly and one early "growl" this week; write what happened.

modules.why: Long term over short term, one big desire, calm, gratitude, identity.
modules.job: Remove one cheap-dopamine source for 7 days and note what you did with the time.

modules.why: Decide with numbers and sources instead of the first story.
modules.job: Record 10 predictions and one decision with a base rate.

modules.why: Prevent trouble and respond safely. No heroics.
modules.job: Two-factor on, 112 plan filled in, a first-aid course booked.

modules.why: Run money and paperwork like an independent adult.
modules.job: A saving rule set and one real credit offer costed.

modules.n: People II: talk, speak, hold a line
modules.why: Conversation, clear speaking, negotiation and boundaries.
modules.job: One prepared difficult conversation, reviewed.

m0.s: It's 20:30. You had a bad school day and you're telling yourself you'll do double tomorrow.
m0.w: Bad days are guaranteed by maths. A bad day where you still dial is a good day. Do the 10 now.

m0.s: You keep the HVAC idea 'open just in case' while calling home care owners.
m0.w: Decide = cut off. Half-open doors stop anything from compounding.

m0.s: Your hands shake before the first dial of the night.
m0.w: Nerves fade with volume, not with more preparation. The first 10 calls are warm-up reps.

m0.s: 'What if nobody ever buys?' keeps you from starting.
m0.w: Fear lives in the vague. Write the actual steps and a plan B; the downside is survivable.

m0.s: An owner hangs up rudely and you want to stop for the night.
m0.w: Mental toughness: how unlikely a bad event is to change your behaviour against your goal. Next dial.

m1.s: You're reading about hiring sales teams while you have zero clients.
m1.w: Study only your stage, plus one before and one after. You are at Improvise/Monetize.

m1.s: You have 6 ideas to improve the business this week. Which one first?
m1.w: Find the one constraint (the first paying agency) and put everything on it.

m1.s: Should you call every home care agency in Florida or one area first?
m1.w: Niche down until it's obvious: Tampa Bay private-pay agencies first, Collier and Lee after 3 paying agencies.

m1.s: You're judging whether caregiver recruiting is a good market at all.
m1.w: Pain, purchasing power, easy to target, growing.

m2.s: Owners say 'sounds good' but don't believe it will work for them.
m2.w: Raise perceived likelihood: proof, guarantee, a specific plan.

m2.s: An owner fears paying and getting caregivers who ghost.
m2.w: A guarantee removes the risk: Stay-or-Replace 90, No-Show Insurance.

m2.s: Everyone tells owners 'we help you hire'. You sound like every agency.
m2.w: Escape the commodity trap: a category of one, a different vehicle and promise.

m2.s: An owner asks for 20% off Priority Bench.
m2.w: Free or full price, never a discount. Offer Pay When They Work or a bonus instead.

m2.s: Your offer has no reason to decide this week.
m2.w: Real scarcity and urgency: max 2 Priority Bench members per town area, Founding 5 price lock.

m3.s: You made 30 dials and booked nothing. You want to change the script.
m3.w: More, then better, then new. Change the script only after 300+ dials on it.

m3.s: An owner replies to your email at 14:00 your time. You answer the next morning.
m3.w: Speed to lead: minutes, not hours. Contact rates fall fast with delay.

m3.s: You call each owner once and give up.
m3.w: 10–14 touches across phone, voicemail and email over a few weeks.

m3.s: A receptionist answers instead of the owner.
m3.w: Treat gatekeepers as allies: be direct, ask for help, sound like you belong.

m3.s: You're wondering which channel to use: ads, content, cold or warm.
m3.w: Core Four. You've picked cold outreach by phone: go deep on one.

m4.s: You feel desperate to get a yes on every call.
m4.w: Detachment: you're sorting, not converting. Your job is the dial, not the yes.

m4.s: Owner: 'Who is this?' and you start a long company intro.
m4.w: One sentence: 'You know how…' then the problem they recognise.

m4.s: Your words are right but owners hang up anyway.
m4.w: Tonality over words: calm, curious, slower, lower.

m4.s: You want the owner to admit hiring is a problem without you claiming it.
m4.w: Poke the bear: a neutral question that makes them doubt the current way.

m4.s: You open with 'How are you today?'
m4.w: Context-first opener: why you're calling them specifically, then permission.

m4.s: Your opener says "we are a caregiver recruiting service". Answered calls end in 15 seconds.
m4.w: Open with the owners' own words about their pain.

m5.s: Owner: 'Hiring is fine.' You move straight to the pitch.
m5.w: Pull teeth: 'Tell me more', 'give me an example' until the real pain shows.

m5.s: Owner says something emotional: 'I'm tired of babysitting new hires.'
m5.w: Label it: 'It sounds like new hires take more of your time than they give back.'

m5.s: You want the owner to talk more without asking a new question.
m5.w: Mirror the last 1–3 words with a curious tone, then stay quiet.

m5.s: You need to know if they can pay and who decides.
m5.w: BANT on the set: budget, authority, need, timing.

m5.s: You want to ask for a commitment without pressure.
m5.w: No-oriented question: 'Would it be a bad idea to send you two profiles?'

m5.s: Owner: "Staffing? It's okay, I guess." You feel the pull to start pitching.
m5.w: Vague means no sale yet. "Can you give me an example?" then "tell me more".

m5.s: Five owners in a row were friendly, had open cases, could decide, and still said "send me something".
m5.w: Criteria are there, desire is not: add education (proof, how it works) before and during.

m6.w: Stall: name the cost of inaction. What happens to the open case while they think?
Money objection = not enough value. Go back to the cost of the problem.

m6.s: Owner: 'We already use a staffing agency.'
m6.w: Acknowledge, then find what they'd improve about the current vendor.

m6.s: You say the price and immediately start explaining.
m6.w: State the price, then 8+ seconds of silence.

m6.s: The call ends with 'I'll get back to you'.
m6.w: Book a meeting from a meeting: put the next step in the calendar now.

m6.s: Owner: "Sounds good, but I need to think about it." You have asked once.
m6.w: Do not argue. "What's your main concern?" then ask again.

m6.s: An owner booked a call for Thursday. Last week two of three booked calls did not show.
m6.w: Process: 6pm and 8am texts with a prepared reason to show.

m6.s: You are writing the one-page explanation of First Hire Free and want a checklist for what must be in it.
m6.w: Gain, relief, cost of waiting, loss of waiting. All true.

m7.s: You want to know if a client is profitable to acquire.
You don't want to spend your own money acquiring clients.
An owner says $2,500 every 4 weeks is too much right now.
m7.w: Downsell, never the same thing for less: Pay When They Work, $1,500 per caregiver who works.

m7.s: A trial agency just got their first caregiver working.
m7.w: Upsell after the first big win: the day-25 results call sells Priority Bench.

m8.s: You want owners to come to you instead of only calling them.
m8.w: A free, complete solution to a narrow problem that reveals the next problem: the Bench Bulletin.

m8.s: Owners show up to calls unprepared and skeptical.
m8.w: A short video before every step: promise, proof, plan.

m8.s: Booked calls convert badly and you don't know where it breaks.
m8.w: Funnel diagnostics: dials → connects → conversations → sets → shows → closes.

m8.s: You can dial 5,000 random listings or 600 private-pay agencies with the owner's direct line.
m8.w: Return per lead, not cost per lead.

m9.s: Friends think the business is a waste and you start doubting.
m9.w: Whose game are you playing? Take advice only from people closer to your goal.

m9.s: Three months in, no client, it feels lonely.
m9.w: The lonely chapter is part of the climb. Keep the work, find better rooms.

m9.s: You compare yourself to Hormozi at $100M.
m9.w: Model the climb, not the summit: what he did at your stage.

m9.s: You're unsure whether to keep going or change the business.
m9.w: Push or pivot: pivot only when real feedback disproves a founding assumption.

m10.s: You're doing every task yourself and drowning.
m10.w: Time study, then delegate the low-value tasks and train.
Hire for workflows, not roles: what exact job gets done?
Prospect, process, product experience + rate of learning, work ethic, humility.

ex.s: It's 20:25. You open War Room 'just to fix one small thing' before dialing.
ex.w: Design the environment: War Room opens on Dial, first number loaded, nothing else open.

ex.s: After a dead block you don't know what to change.
ex.w: Debrief: what worked, what didn't, change one thing.

ex.s: After 2 bad days you want to switch to the HVAC idea tonight.
ex.w: Never decide in an emotional state. Park it for the 8 Dec review.

ex.s: You 'feel like you worked a lot' this week.
ex.w: Track the truth: count dials and conversations, not feelings.

ex.s: You want to "improve the script" this week.
ex.w: Make it a bet: if X then Y, then check both.

mk.s: Owner: 'We get plenty of applicants on Indeed.'
mk.w: Applicants are only one of five systems. Ask where they lose people: selection, week one, month three.

mk.s: Owner: 'Our new hires keep quitting in the first month.'
mk.w: The first-90-day leak. Lead with Stay-or-Replace 90.

mk.s: Owner wants you plus two other recruiters on the same case.
mk.w: Multi-listed orders split commitment; offer to own the hardest case exclusively.

mk.s: You're tempted to set up automations before your first agency.
mk.w: Do things that don't scale: by hand first.

lg.s: You're deciding whether to add a second business idea.
lg.w: Circle of competence: it goes on the too-hard pile until 100 owner conversations.

lg.s: A partner offers referrals if you pay them per client.
lg.w: Per-client payments are a bad incentive and illegal for you. Flat, legal deals only.

lg.s: You want a plan that avoids the obvious ways to fail by July.
lg.w: Invert: list what guarantees failure and avoid it.

l1.s: You slept 5 hours after a late night. Tomorrow you plan to sleep in until 9.
l1.w: After a bad night, change nothing: up at 05:20, no nap, bed 21:00.

l1.s: Energy drink at 18:00 before the dial block.
l1.w: Caffeine before noon; late caffeine steals deep sleep.

l2.s: You missed yesterday's BAC block. You think the week is ruined.
l2.w: Never miss twice: do the minimum version today.

l2.s: You keep skipping the evening stretch.
l2.w: Make it obvious, attractive, easy, satisfying (or shrink it).

l3.s: You reread your history notes three times and feel ready.
l3.w: Rereading feels like learning. Close the notes and recall.

l3.s: You practise 20 problems of the same type in a row.
l3.w: Interleave: mix problem types, like the exam.

l4.s: You do sprints right after a hard circuit.
l4.w: Power is trained fresh with full rest.

l4.s: Your weight jumped 1.2 kg overnight and you think the bulk is going too fast.
l4.w: Judge by the 7-day average, not one morning.

l5.s: Your serve shoulder aches after long sessions.
l5.w: Train the decelerators ~3x/week, and see a physio if it persists.

l5.s: You keep telling yourself 'don't miss' and miss more.
l5.w: Self 1 interference. Give the mind a notice task instead.

l6.s: You want an owner to reply to your email, so you send the free Bench Bulletin first.
A chatty owner suddenly gives one-word answers.
l6.w: Anomaly against the baseline: something changed. Ask.

l7.s: An hour of 'improving the app' instead of the dial block.
l7.w: Fake work: it feels productive and avoids the hard thing. Long term over short term.

l7.s: You slide back to skipping calls a week after a great day.
l7.w: Identity thermostat: raise the set point with repeated votes, not one great day.

m11.s: You earn more than you spend for the first time.
m11.w: Margin: income > expenses for 90 days is milestone one.

m11.s: You want a safety net before investing.
m11.w: Optionality: 6–12 months of essentials in a separate account.

m11.s: Fees and inflation quietly eat your savings.
m11.w: The money monsters: inflation, taxes, interruption, fees.

l8.s: After two rude owners you are sure "Tampa hates cold calls".
l8.w: Two calls are not a rate. What do your last 100 dials say?

l8.s: A video says the BAC written exams start on 14 June.
l8.w: Trace it: that is Romania's calendar. Moldova's is on ance.gov.md.

l8.s: You plan a 25-minute block that has taken 35 minutes the last four times.
l8.w: Plan with your real factor and a buffer.

l9.s: An SMS from "your bank": card blocked, confirm within one hour through this link.
l9.w: All four signs. Stop and call the number on the card.

l9.s: A man at the bus stop is unconscious. People are filming.
l9.w: Call 112, location first, follow the operator.

l10.s: A shop offers a phone for "only 450 lei a month".
l10.w: Total repaid and DAE, not the monthly payment.

l10.s: You were paid for the month of lessons and plan to save "what is left".
l10.w: Decide the saving first, on payday.

l11.s: A parent insists: "Move my son to the Green group this week." There is no space.
l11.w: Ask why: the interest may be match play or a friend, and has other solutions.

l11.s: A teammate keeps asking you to cover his sessions during your dial block.

spot.s: "Hi, how are you doing today? I'm Egor from Caregiver Bench, we are a leading recruiting solution that…"
o: Opens with small talk and a company pitch instead of context + permission

spot.s: "I know you're busy, I'll be super quick, I promise, can I have just 2 minutes, please?"
o: Begging tone kills status; ask permission calmly once

spot.s: Owner: "Hiring is OK." You: "Great! So let me tell you how we work."
o: Accepts a surface answer; pull teeth with 'tell me more'

spot.s: "Do you have problems with hiring? Do you need caregivers? Would you like more?"
o: Stacked closed questions; ask one open 'how/what' question

spot.s: "It's $2,500 every 4 weeks… but honestly we can be flexible, and it pays for itself, and…"
o: Talks after the price; state it and stay silent

spot.s: Owner: "Let me think about it." You: "Sure, I'll call you next week!"
o: Accepts a stall with no booked next step (BAMFAM, cost of inaction)

spot.s: Owner: "Too expensive." You: "OK, I can do $1,800."
o: Discounts the core offer; go back to value or a real downsell

spot.s: "We charge $200 for every family we help you take on."
o: Per-family/client charges break the Florida Patient Brokering Act line; recruit-only, flat fees

spot.s: Owner: "Hiring is a bit hard." You: "Great, so here is how Caregiver Bench works…"
o: Pitches after a vague answer instead of asking for an example

spot.s: Owner: "I have to ask my partner." You: "But you said staffing was urgent, so that doesn't make sense."
o: Tells the owner he is wrong instead of asking the main concern

spot.s: Text before a booked call: "Hi! Just a reminder about our call tomorrow. Looking forward to it!"
o: A reminder with no reason to show

risk.s: An owner says: 'Pay you per family we sign thanks to your caregivers? Sure, $200 each.'
o: Decline: no per-family/client/referral fees (Florida Patient Brokering Act); flat recruiting fees only
Accept but call it a bonus
risk.w: Never charge per family, client, lead or referral. Recruit only, flat fees.

risk.s: An owner asks: 'Are your caregivers background-checked?' You haven't checked anyone.
o: Say plainly you don't run background or reference checks; the agency runs its own as the employer
Say yes, to keep the deal moving
risk.w: Never claim a check that didn't happen. FCRA: you don't do reference or background checks.

risk.s: Closing a trial: you're tempted to say you already have 20 caregivers on the bench. You have 3.
o: Say the real number and how you source to their case
Avoid numbers and imply it's large
risk.w: Honesty is the foundation. A lie on call one kills the 50-year tower.

risk.s: An owner offers to let a caregiver start working for a family through you directly.
o: Decline: you recruit for the agency; the agency employs (W-2) and places caregivers
Ask the family to pay you
risk.w: Recruit only. Never employ, place or send caregivers to families.

risk.s: To save time you want to record calls to review them later.
o: Don't record calls; take notes right after instead
risk.w: No call recording. Write a 2-line debrief after each conversation.

risk.s: A caregiver applicant asks what it costs her to join your bench.
o: A share of her first paycheck
